cards.canonical_statement: For any actual curve c with velocity u on uIcc(a,b) and any scalar one-form field D, the pullback is interval-integrable from a to b if and only if it is integrable from b to a. Reversing the oriented parameter interval negates its integral. The total integral identity alone does not assert integrability.
cards.proof_strategy: Identify the pullback t↦D(c(t))(u(t)) using the stated actual velocity.
sketch_steps: Identify the pullback t↦D(c(t))(u(t)) using the stated actual velocity.
The same unordered interval underlies both integration directions.
Interval integrability is therefore unchanged by reversing endpoints.
The oriented interval integral changes sign, including the zero-length case.

cards.canonical_statement: For any differentiable curve c with velocity u and any one-form D, integrability of the pullback on a..b and b..e implies that the sum of these two oriented line integrals equals its integral on a..e. No ordering of a,b,e is required.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the same parameterized curve and pullback on both intervals.
sketch_steps: Use the same parameterized curve and pullback on both intervals.
Retain interval integrability separately on a..b and b..e.
Apply additivity of interval integrals across the common parameter b.
The oriented identity remains valid without assuming that b lies between a and e.

cards.canonical_statement: For every dimension n with coordinate i, base vector x, distinct real endpoints a,b, and constant velocity u(t)=e_i, the curve obtained by replacing coordinate i of x by t has actual velocity u. Integrating the exact coordinate form dx_i along this curve from a to b differs from integrating it from b to a.
cards.proof_strategy: The derivative of the coordinate-update curve is the chosen basis vector e_i.
sketch_steps: The derivative of the coordinate-update curve is the chosen basis vector e_i.
The derivative of the coordinate potential y↦y_i is coordinate projection.
Applying this coordinate form to e_i gives the constant scalar pullback 1.
The oriented integrals equal b-a and a-b; equality would force a=b, contrary to the hypothesis.

cards.canonical_statement: Let B be any continuous bilinear real form on ℝⁿ, and let D(x)(y)=B(x,y). For curves c,d with actual velocities u,w on uIcc(a,b), if B(c(t),w(t)) and B(u(t),d(t)) are interval-integrable, the sum of their oriented integrals equals B(c(b),d(b))-B(c(a),d(a)). This is integration by parts for a pair of vector-valued curves; B need not be symmetric.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the supplied pointwise equality D(x)(y)=B(x,y) to identify both scalar contractions.
sketch_steps: Use the supplied pointwise equality D(x)(y)=B(x,y) to identify both scalar contractions.
Differentiate t↦B(c(t),d(t)) by the bilinear product rule.
The derivative is B(c(t),w(t))+B(u(t),d(t)), preserving the order of both slots.
The separate integrability hypotheses justify adding the integrals and applying the fundamental theorem.
Evaluate the bilinear primitive at the two oriented endpoints.
